## The question

[newenvironment/newcommand for existing environment in LaTeX-Beamer](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/16654/newenvironment-newcommand-for-existing-environment-in-latex-beamer), asked by [Julian](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/14906/julian) on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-04-26; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I would like to have [the solution of highlighting a line in `listings`-package][q-1]  as a command or environment. To bad I cannot get it working. I tried:
>
>  * a simple `newenvironment`: compile errors
>  * `\newcommand`: also compile errors
>  * the [`environ`-package][q-2], see below
>
>         \NewEnviron{listingh}{
>           \vspace{-\baselineskip}
>           \begin{lstlisting}[backgroundcolor=\color{yellow}]
>           \BODY
>           \end{lstlisting}
>           \vspace{-\baselineskip}
>         }
>
> Also, same kind of errors. `missing {`, `missing number, threaded a zero` etc.
>
> I try to use it with the `beamer`-package and `pdflatex`.
>
>
>   [q-1]: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/1304315/highlighting-a-chunk-of-code-within-a-lstlisting/1313704#1313704
>   [q-2]: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/1872951/wrap-latex-command-in-environment/1877976#1877976
:::

In addition to Martin's answer, you need to take special care within the beamer class, because that class also drastically alters LaTeX's expansion habits.  See section 2.6 of the beamer manual.

```latex
\documentclass{beamer}
\usepackage{listings}

\lstnewenvironment{listingh}[1][]{%
    \vspace{-\baselineskip}%
    \lstset{backgroundcolor=\color{yellow},#1}%
}{%
    \vspace{-\baselineskip}%
}


\begin{document}

\defverbatim[colored]\mycode{%
\begin{listingh}[emph={PRINT,GOTO},emphstyle={\color{blue}}]
10 PRINT "HELLO, WORLD!"
20 GOTO 10
\end{listingh} }


\begin{frame}{BASIC}
\mycode
\end{frame}

% or
\begin{frame}[fragile]{C++}
\begin{listingh}[emph={cout,for},emphstyle={\color{blue}}]
for (;;) {
    cout << "Hello, world!";
}
\end{listingh}

\end{document}
```

This looks bad but keep in mind you can redefine `\mycode` over and over again before each frame.
